# KD-real observables are generated by KD-positive pure states

Status: `candidate_full_likely_valid`.

Source: Matéo Spriet, *Characterizing the Kirkwood–Dirac positivity on
second countable LCA groups*, arXiv:2507.23628, Conjecture (11).

## Full result

For every second-countable locally compact abelian group `G`, the real vector
space of KD-real self-adjoint Hilbert–Schmidt observables is exactly the
Hilbert–Schmidt closure of the real span of KD-positive pure states:

```text
V_KDr = closure(span_R(E_KD+^pure)).
```

The proof uses the source's unitary characteristic-function transform and
support lemma.  Up to null sets, the commuting phase-space locus

```text
N = {(g,chi): chi(g)=1}
```

is a countable union of compact-open rectangles `H x H^perp`.  On each such
rectangle, the characteristic functions of the Weyl translates of the Haar
projector are all Fourier characters, hence an orthonormal basis.  Density on
the union and self-adjoint symmetrization finish the proof.

The separate convex-hull conjecture for KD-positive mixed states is not
claimed.

## Reproduction

Run the finite phase-space consistency check with:

```bash
conda run --no-capture-output -n sandbox python \
  code/verify_finite_phase_space_span.py
```

The script exhaustively enumerates subgroups for eight small finite abelian
groups and verifies that the pure-state characteristic functions have rank
exactly `|N|`.
